messages.author: 881c51ed14655bd5
messages.subject: RNG with .parallel
parts:
I'm intentionally trying to break plyr with random number generation
and found that it did a bit of unexpected behavior, probably what it
should do but not what I expected.

---
> library(foreach)
> library(doSNOW)
> cl<- makeSOCKcluster(2)
> registerDoSNOW(cl)
> clusterEvalQ(cl, set.seed(12345))
[[1]]
NULL

[[2]]
NULL

> clusterEvalQ(cl, rnorm(5))
[[1]]
[1] 0.5855288 0.7094660 -0.1093033 -0.4534972 0.6058875

[[2]]
[1] 0.5855288 0.7094660 -0.1093033 -0.4534972 0.6058875

> alply(c(5,5),1, rnorm)
$`1`
[1] 0.83465573 -0.10478436 1.24042984 0.03336694 0.72424390

$`2`
[1] -1.4935661 0.3888823 0.5115154 -0.6403826 -0.1741089

attr(,"split_type")
[1] "array"
attr(,"split_labels")
X1
1 1
2 2
---

I was expecting the results to be the same. I could not find any
documentation that plyr sets a parallel seed, but that is what is
apparently happening. Could I get confirmation that this is intended
behavior? If it is it should be documented.

Thanks,
Andrew Redd

messages.author: 3d3472d11b922fc3
messages.subject: Re: RNG with .parallel
parts:
You might be getting burned by seed locking to CPU and not to "compute
process" -- but I've not used the do* packages, just the snow and
snowFT packages. See the snowFT package for a more stable / completely
reproducible example, and also you should consider one of the parallel
RNG's (rsprng or rlecuyer).
